title: SolarAlign Field Data Worksheet
subtitle: Collect the roof, solar, utility, and project information needed for a transparent timing and value analysis.
instructions: Write down the source for every answer. Estimates are useful, but label them as estimates. Attach roof reports, proposals, utility bills, and production studies where available.

sections.title: Project and building context
sections.description: These details identify the project and help the team verify that later estimates apply to the right building. They do not directly change the current calculation unless noted.

fields.label: Project or building name
fields.note: A clear name for this analysis.
fields.importance: Keeps reports, source documents, and calculation results tied to the same project.
fields.source_hint: Owner, facility team, or project file

fields.label: Building address
fields.note: Street address, city, state, and ZIP code.
fields.importance: Location affects solar resource, utility territory, rates, permitting, and incentive eligibility, even though this version accepts annual production as an input.

fields.label: Project / facilities contact
fields.note: Name, role, phone, or email for the person coordinating information.
fields.importance: Makes it possible to resolve missing roof, utility, and proposal facts before a decision is made.

fields.label: Site visit or report date
fields.note: The date the roof or property information was observed or reported.
fields.importance: Roof condition and cost estimates age over time; recording the date helps reviewers judge whether information is current.

fields.label: Usable roof area
fields.note: Approximate unobstructed roof area potentially available for solar.
fields.importance: Useful roof area helps a designer estimate feasible system size. It is contextual here because the current engine uses annual kWh from a production study.
fields.source_hint: Roof plan, aerial measurement, or solar proposal

fields.label: Proposed solar system size
fields.note: The direct-current nameplate capacity of the proposed array.
fields.importance: System size connects roof area, project cost, and energy production and is essential when validating a production or cost estimate.

fields.label: Roof type / membrane
fields.note: For example: TPO, EPDM, modified bitumen, metal, or built-up roof.
fields.importance: Roof type affects attachment method, compatibility, warranty coordination, installation effort, and future removal work.
fields.source_hint: Roof report, warranty, or maintenance records

fields.label: Estimated remaining roof life
fields.note: Record a range if the report gives one; do not turn a range into an exact fact.
fields.importance: Helps the team choose a roof-replacement scenario and decide whether solar should wait, proceed now, or be coordinated with reroofing.

fields.label: Inspection limitations
fields.note: Record areas not accessed, tests not performed, concealed conditions, and other limits on the available roof evidence.
fields.importance: Makes uncertainty visible so a preliminary financial result is not mistaken for a complete roof or structural assessment.

fields.label: Structural capacity review status
fields.note: State whether rooftop solar loading has been assessed, by whom, and when.
fields.importance: Financial results do not prove physical feasibility. A qualified structural review is needed before installation.
fields.source_hint: Structural engineer or property condition report

sections.title: Roof and solar costs
sections.description: These figures determine when cash is spent and whether coordinating roof work with solar avoids future disruption.

fields.label: Selected roof replacement timing
fields.note: The planning year used for comparison: 0 means now, 3 means three years from now.
fields.importance: Sets the roof-only baseline, the installation date for the roof-then-solar plan, and the year of panel removal and downtime if solar goes first.
fields.source_hint: Roof assessment plus project-team planning decision

fields.label: Roof replacement cost
fields.note: Expected total cost for one roof replacement in consistent dollars.
fields.importance: The engine charges this cost once in every plan. Paying it earlier changes its present value and can change which timing plan is viable.
fields.source_hint: Qualified contractor budget or capital plan

fields.label: Solar removal and reinstallation cost
fields.note: Cost to safely detach, store, and reinstall the array during future roof work.
fields.importance: Applies when solar is installed before the roof is replaced and directly reduces that plan's project-side NPV.
fields.source_hint: Solar installer or qualified contractor allowance

fields.label: Solar installation cost
fields.note: Total installed capital cost before incentives unless the source clearly states otherwise.
fields.importance: This is the largest upfront solar cash outflow and strongly affects whether any timing plan creates positive long-term value.
fields.source_hint: Solar proposal with scope and exclusions

fields.label: Annual operations and maintenance cost
fields.note: Expected yearly inspection, monitoring, service, and maintenance cost.
fields.importance: The engine subtracts this in each operating year, so omitting it would overstate project value.
fields.source_hint: Service proposal, asset manager, or benchmark

fields.label: Production lost during roof work
fields.note: Estimated share of annual production lost while panels are removed and reinstalled.
fields.importance: Reduces electricity value in the roof-work year for the solar-first plan.

sections.title: Energy production and value
sections.description: These inputs describe how much electricity the array is expected to make and what that electricity is worth over time.

fields.label: First-year annual solar production
fields.note: Expected alternating-current electricity in the first full operating year.
fields.importance: The engine multiplies production by electricity value to calculate yearly benefits. Use a site-specific study such as PVWatts or a proposal estimate.

fields.label: Electricity value
fields.note: The assumed value of each solar kWh, based on the applicable rate or credit treatment.
fields.importance: Converts production into dollar value. Utility tariff, meter arrangement, and credit rules can materially change it.
fields.source_hint: Utility bills, tariff, or documented modeling assumption

fields.label: Annual panel degradation
fields.note: Expected yearly decline in panel output.
fields.importance: Reduces generation in later years so lifetime value is not overstated.

fields.label: Annual electricity-value escalation
fields.note: Expected annual change in the real value of electricity.
fields.importance: Changes the dollar value of future generation. Use zero when modeling in constant dollars without real escalation.

fields.label: Utility provider and rate class
fields.note: Name the utility, tariff, and account class if known.
fields.importance: Needed to verify the value assigned to solar electricity and whether credits can be allocated as assumed.

fields.label: Meter configuration
fields.note: Describe master meters, separate tenant meters, common-area meters, and account holders.
fields.importance: Determines where solar production can offset usage and who can actually receive bill credits.
fields.source_hint: Single-line diagram, bills, or facilities team

fields.label: Who pays each electric bill?
fields.note: List the party responsible for each relevant meter or account.
fields.importance: Makes the value-allocation issue visible and helps the team design a structure that supports adoption instead of leaving savings stranded.

sections.title: Analysis assumptions and value alignment
sections.description: These settings control the comparison period and show how usable solar value could reach project sponsors and building users.

fields.label: Share of allocatable value reaching occupants / electricity users
fields.note: Starting scenario for the share of usable electricity value assigned to building users rather than the project/capital side.
fields.importance: Does not change generation; it changes the modeled distribution of value and helps identify shares where both modeled outcomes are positive.

fields.label: Value not currently assignable
fields.note: Share of electricity value that cannot yet be assigned to either modeled side.
fields.importance: Captures uncertainty, unusable credits, or unmatched load before the remaining value is divided.

fields.label: Analysis horizon
fields.note: Number of future years included in the comparison.
fields.importance: Controls how many years of production, maintenance, and planned roof activity are counted.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.note: Rate used to translate future project-side cash flows into today's dollars.
fields.importance: A higher rate gives less weight to distant savings and can change the preferred timing plan and NPV.
